phase1_inventory.scientific_basis: Exact-diagonalization model: spinless fermions on a periodic one-dimensional L-site lattice with nearest-neighbor interaction V=2, nearest- and next-nearest-neighbor hopping t=t'=1, and independent zero-mean Gaussian onsite potentials of variance W^2; the sampled disorder vector is rescaled/restricted so sum_i w_i^2/L equals W^2 exactly.

phase1_inventory.source_ref: Sec. II, p. 2, paragraph after Eq. (1)
phase1_inventory.scientific_basis: Empirical ensemble claim: fixing each realization's mean-square disorder exactly to W^2 reduces statistical uncertainty by about a factor of two for the largest samples, changes spectral statistics mainly for 4 <= W <= 9, but does not qualitatively change the reported finite-size behavior.

Numerical protocol claim: all eigenenergies in the half-filled sector (L/2 particles) are weighted equally; sizes extend through L=16; about 10,000 disorder realizations are used at L=8, about 50-100 at L=14 and 16 away from the putative critical region, and 1,000 per W in that region.

phase1_inventory.source_ref: Sec. III, p. 3, equations defining delta_n and r_n
phase1_inventory.scientific_basis: For ordered many-body energies, delta_n=E_(n+1)-E_n >= 0 and r_n=min(delta_n,delta_(n-1))/max(delta_n,delta_(n-1)), constrained to 0 <= r_n <= 1; the reported observable r(W,L) is the all-state spectral mean followed by a disorder mean.

phase1_inventory.source_ref: Sec. III, p. 3, paragraph before Fig. 1
phase1_inventory.scientific_basis: Analytic Poisson benchmark: P_P(r)=2/(1+r)^2 on 0 <= r <= 1 and mean <r>_P=2 ln 2 - 1 approximately 0.386.

phase1_inventory.source_ref: Sec. III, p. 3 and Ref. 17 note, p. 5
phase1_inventory.scientific_basis: Numerical GOE benchmark: <r>_GOE=0.5295 +/- 0.0006, P_GOE(r) vanishes linearly as r approaches zero, and the plotted benchmark was generated from 1,000 random matrices of dimension 3,432 (the half-filled L=14 Hilbert-space dimension).

Full probability distributions P(r) for the analytic Poisson reference, a numerical GOE reference, and the interacting-fermion model at L=16 for W=3 (diffusive), W=7 (intermediate), and W=11 (localized); the limiting small-r and distribution-shape comparisons are numerical targets.

phase1_inventory.source_ref: Sec. IV, p. 3, paragraph before Fig. 2
phase1_inventory.scientific_basis: Numerical sweep and uncertainty claim: with t=t'=V/2=1, W is scanned from 1 through 10 or higher; r(W,L) is the disorder average of each sample's all-spectrum mean, and its plotted uncertainty is sqrt(([<r>^2]-[<r>]^2)/(R-1)).

phase1_inventory.source_ref: Figure 2 upper panel and caption, p. 3
phase1_inventory.scientific_basis: Full-range r(W,L) curves with error bars for L=8, 10, 12, 14, and 16 across the displayed disorder range; the caption specifies their top-to-bottom ordering at large W and that hidden error bars are smaller than the plotted points.

phase1_inventory.source_ref: Figure 2 lower panel and caption, p. 3
phase1_inventory.scientific_basis: Enlarged r(W,L) view of the W approximately 4-8 crossing region for L=8, 10, 12, 14, and 16, intended to resolve the locations and systematic drift of adjacent-size crossings.

phase1_inventory.source_ref: Sec. IV, pp. 3-4, first paragraph after Fig. 2
phase1_inventory.scientific_basis: Data interpretation claim: for W>8, increasing L makes the statistics more Poisson-like; for W<4, increasing L moves the statistics toward GOE; the complete P(r) distributions in these regimes are also claimed to approach the Poisson and GOE benchmarks.

phase1_inventory.source_ref: Sec. IV, pp. 3-4, first paragraph after Fig. 2
phase1_inventory.scientific_basis: Finite-size clean-limit claim: momentum-sector decoupling suppresses mean r below the GOE value at very weak disorder; chains shorter than eight sites retain this effect to larger W, L=8 shows a remnant at W=1, and larger displayed L values do not over the studied W range.

phase1_inventory.source_ref: Sec. IV, p. 4, paragraph beginning 'The simplest one-parameter'
phase1_inventory.scientific_basis: Finite-size trend claim: crossings of adjacent-L r(W,L) curves shift systematically toward larger W and smaller r as L increases, while the curves sharpen; this observed drift is said to obstruct straightforward one-parameter finite-size scaling.

phase1_inventory.source_ref: Sec. IV, p. 4, paragraph beginning 'The simplest one-parameter'
phase1_inventory.scientific_basis: Unplotted numerical robustness claim: varying temperature, interaction, filling, spectral statistic, and spectral window can reduce the crossing drift (especially tail trimming or lower temperature), but none of the explored changes eliminates or reverses it.

phase1_inventory.source_ref: Sec. IV, p. 4, paragraphs beginning 'Although at this point'
phase1_inventory.scientific_basis: Quantitative extrapolation claim: the finite-size data are described as consistent with a finite limiting W_c and r_c(L) approaching the Poisson value 2 ln 2 - 1, while the competing W_c=infinity scenario cannot be excluded; the paper explicitly does not resolve between these limits.

independent_checks.claim: Independent quadrature gives Poisson normalization 1.0000000000002918 and mean 0.38629436111972393, agreeing with 2 ln 2 - 1.
reproduction_steps: Integrate 2/(1+r)^2 and r*2/(1+r)^2 from r=0 to 1 on a 1,000,001-point grid and compare the latter to 2*ln(2)-1.

independent_checks.claim: Independent GOE matrices gave means 0.53812 (80x128), 0.53272 (96x256), 0.52837 (32x512), and 0.53068 (8x1024), bracketing and converging toward the printed 0.5295 within sampling error.
reproduction_steps: For each declared size/sample pair, generate real Gaussian A, diagonalize (A+A.T)/sqrt(2N), compute consecutive-gap ratios, and average using seeds 9173-9176.

independent_checks.claim: A tuple-occupation implementation of creation/annihilation signs, independent of the bundled bit implementation, reproduced weak/intermediate/strong mean ordering at L=8 and L=10 and matched the bundled L=8 Hamiltonian exactly for a fixed disorder vector.
reproduction_steps: Enumerate sorted occupied-site tuples; apply annihilation and creation signs from tuple positions; build Eq. (1); compare the L=8 clean and fixed-disorder matrices and eigenvalues elementwise.

falsification_attempts.hypothesis: The Poisson/GOE reference values and weak-to-strong disorder ordering are internally plausible.
reproduction_steps: Repeat the independent GOE size sweep and tuple-basis ED without importing bundled numerical routines or arrays.

discrepancy.paper_claim: L=16 curves at W=3,7,11 and GOE 1000x3432
discrepancy.reproduction_result: L=12 curves with 32 realizations and GOE 96x512
discrepancy.gap: System size, sample count, and GOE matrix campaign are reduced.
discrepancy.tolerance_basis: Exact figure parameters are a hard gate; qualitative ordering cannot substitute for L=16 and 1000x3432.

target_reviews.assessment_reason: The generated full-disorder curves omit L=16 and use 160/64/32/2 samples for L=8/10/12/14, far below the paper's printed anchors and critical-region schedule. The attested run is a feature-scale campaign, while missing printed W-grid and L=10/12 counts were reconstructed rather than recovered as paper-exact inputs.
target_reviews.direct_cause: The generated full-disorder curves omit L=16 and use 160/64/32/2 samples for L=8/10/12/14, far below the paper's printed anchors and critical-region schedule.
target_reviews.root_cause: The attested run is a feature-scale campaign, while missing printed W-grid and L=10/12 counts were reconstructed rather than recovered as paper-exact inputs.

independent_checks.claim: Independent tuple-basis ED gave decreasing mean r from W=3 to 7 to 11 at L=8 (0.51279,0.46120,0.43738) and L=10 (0.51871,0.43989,0.41081), so the broad crossover survives a different implementation and seeds.
reproduction_steps: Build Eq. (1) from occupied-site tuples, normalize each independent Gaussian disorder vector to RMS W, diagonalize every full half-filled spectrum, and average 72 L=8 and 36 L=10 realizations at W=3,7,11.

independent_checks.claim: Independent and bundled Hamiltonians are real symmetric and give identical L=8 matrices/eigenvalues for a fixed explicit disorder vector; dimensions C(8,4)=70, C(14,7)=3432, C(16,8)=12870 are correct.
reproduction_steps: Construct the matrix independently from tuple creation/annihilation operations and compare Hermiticity, dimensions, entries, and eigenvalues.

falsification_attempts.hypothesis: Every tested size crosses broadly from GOE-like toward Poisson-like statistics as W increases.
reproduction_steps: Run independent tuple-basis ED at L=8 and 10 for W=3,7,11 with independent seeds and compare distances from 0.5295 and 2 ln 2 - 1.

discrepancy.paper_source: Figure 2 upper panel and Sec. II sample-count paragraph
discrepancy.paper_claim: Curves for L=8,10,12,14,16 with paper sampling
discrepancy.reproduction_result: Curves for L=8,10,12,14 only, with L=14 based on two realizations
discrepancy.gap: One required size is absent and sampling is reduced by orders of magnitude.
discrepancy.tolerance_basis: All plotted sizes and paper-scale sampling/convergence are required for figure reproduction.

target_reviews.assessment_reason: The enlarged crossing dataset omits L=16, has no sign-changing L=8/10 crossing in W=4-8, and has three sign changes each for L=10/12 and L=12/14 because of reduced-sample noise. The crossing estimator substitutes a nearest approach when no crossing exists and then selects whichever of multiple crossings lies closest to W=6; the essential gate counts output rows rather than validating unique physical crossings.

target_reviews.root_cause: The crossing estimator substitutes a nearest approach when no crossing exists and then selects whichever of multiple crossings lies closest to W=6; the essential gate counts output rows rather than validating unique physical crossings.

independent_checks.claim: A continuous-curve crossing in a sampled interval requires a sign change (or exact zero) of r_upper-r_lower. The L=8/10 difference is negative at every W from 4 to 8, so the reported W=4 entry is not a crossing.
reproduction_steps: Join level_ratio_curves.csv by W; compute r_10-r_8 for W=4,4.5,...,8; verify all nine values are negative; compare with the nearest_approach_no_sign_change label.

independent_checks.claim: Three independent reduced-scale seed sweeps produced 0-3 L=8/10 crossings and 1-4 L=10/12 crossings in W=4-8, demonstrating that low-sample crossing identities are not stable.
reproduction_steps: Using the independent tuple-basis ED, repeat W=4:0.5:8 curves three times with new seeds and 48/24/4 samples for L=8/10/12; enumerate every sign change without a nearest-approach fallback.

falsification_attempts.hypothesis: All three adjacent-size rows constitute resolved crossings suitable for the Figure 2 lower-panel drift analysis.
reproduction_steps: Check the sign-change invariant for every adjacent pair and list all intersections rather than selecting the one nearest W=6.

discrepancy.paper_source: Figure 2 lower panel and Sec. IV crossing discussion
discrepancy.paper_claim: Resolved adjacent-size crossings drift with L
discrepancy.reproduction_result: One nearest approach, plus three possible crossings for each of the other two pairs, from an L=16-free reduced run
discrepancy.gap: Crossing identity and required size coverage are unresolved.
discrepancy.tolerance_basis: A crossing must have a sign change and remain stable under sampling refinement; nearest approach is not equivalent.

target_reviews.assessment_reason: The reported monotone sequence begins with a non-crossing nearest approach and depends on arbitrary selection among multiple noisy crossings; no convergence or statistical robustness evidence is supplied. The acceptance check tests only the peak-to-peak range of selected W values, not increasing W, decreasing r, unique crossing identity, uncertainty, or stability under more samples/seeds.

independent_checks.claim: Independent seed sweeps at comparable reduced precision changed both the number and locations of sign-change crossings, so the generated three-point drift is not a stable numerical result.
reproduction_steps: Repeat independent L=8/10/12 curves for three fresh seeds on W=4:0.5:8 and enumerate all sign changes; compare crossing multiplicities and positions across repeats.

independent_checks.claim: The implemented CHK_CROSSING_DRIFT accepts any nonzero range and never tests the paper's two directional predicates; CHK_CROSSING_ROWS accepts a fallback row even without a crossing.
reproduction_steps: Inspect the two checks: verify CHK_CROSSING_ROWS uses row count and CHK_CROSSING_DRIFT uses only peak-to-peak W; compare those predicates with the target claim in contracts/target_claims.json.

falsification_attempts.hypothesis: The reduced generated crossings robustly reproduce drift toward larger W and lower r.
reproduction_steps: Run the independent seed sweep and apply only genuine sign-change crossings; reject nearest approaches and do not choose a crossing by distance to W=6.

discrepancy.paper_claim: Adjacent-size crossings systematically move to larger W and smaller r
discrepancy.reproduction_result: Selected values 4.0/0.4972, 5.7404/0.4573, 6.9168/0.4391, where the first is not a crossing and later pairs each have multiple crossings
discrepancy.gap: The apparent direction is not a converged or uniquely defined crossing sequence.
discrepancy.tolerance_basis: Direction must be evaluated on genuine, unique or uncertainty-resolved crossings and survive increased sampling/seeds.

findings.claim: Authored numerical scope contains only four entries and omits eleven independently inventoried quantitative claims. No targets were invented for the omissions.
findings.direct_cause: contracts/numerical_scope_claims.json enumerates only the three figure panels and one drift claim.
findings.root_cause: Authored coverage was figure-led rather than a full paper quantitative-claim ledger.
reproduction_steps: List contracts/numerical_scope_claims.json .numeric_items[].item_id.
Independently scan Eq. (1), Secs. II-IV, figure captions, and Ref. 17 note in paper/paper-source/OandHfinal.tex.
Compare both ID sets against protocol.phase1_inventory and confirm the eleven unmatched numeric rows.

findings.claim: All four targets are backed only by the explicitly reduced-scale v2 run; no paper-exact attested execution exists.
findings.direct_cause: parameters_paper_exact is false; Figure 1 uses L=12 and reduced GOE; Figure 2 omits L=16 and severely reduces samples.
findings.root_cause: The available run was bounded for local compute, while the complete original W grid and L=10/12 realization counts are not printed.
reproduction_steps: Read actual_parameters in the v2 attestation and compare them with the paper values in paper/paper-source/OandHfinal.tex.
Confirm that no paper-scale attestation or paper-scale generated data appear in bundle_manifest.json.

findings.claim: The L=8/10 row is explicitly a nearest approach with no sign change, not a crossing.
findings.direct_cause: r_10-r_8 stays negative at all nine W points from 4 to 8, but crossing_estimates always returns a fallback row.
findings.root_cause: The data contract permits nearest_approach_no_sign_change to satisfy the crossing-row gate.
reproduction_steps: Compute r_10(W)-r_8(W) for W=4,4.5,...,8 from level_ratio_curves.csv and verify no zero or sign change.
Inspect crossing_drift.csv and confirm its first method is nearest_approach_no_sign_change.

findings.claim: The crossing/drift checks cannot establish the claimed direction or robustness.
findings.direct_cause: The two remaining adjacent pairs each have three sign changes, L=14 has only two realizations, and the gate checks only row count and peak-to-peak W range.
findings.root_cause: No convergence criterion, unique-crossing rule, directional predicate, or uncertainty-aware test was encoded.
reproduction_steps: Enumerate every sign change for L=10/12 and L=12/14 from W=4 to 8; obtain three for each pair.
Inspect aggregate() and verify that it chooses the crossing closest to W=6, then applies only row-count and peak-to-peak tests.
Repeat reduced independent curves with fresh seeds and observe changing crossing multiplicities.

findings.claim: Reduced-config provenance over-attributes reconstructed numerical choices to the paper caption.
findings.direct_cause: The provenance row cites the caption for the full w_values and histogram objects, although half-step W values and 40 bins are unprinted choices and model_length=12 contradicts Figure 1's printed L=16.
findings.root_cause: Parameter provenance is grouped at object level instead of tracing each claim-relevant field separately.
reproduction_steps: Expand reduced_scale.json histogram and w_values fields.
Compare each field with Figure 1/2 captions and text.
Verify that L=12, 40 bins, and the complete half-step grid are not paper-caption parameters.

findings.claim: The render contract describes T001 GOE scope as 32x256 while the attested v2 data use 96x512.
findings.direct_cause: implementation/config/render_contract.json retained v1 scope text after v2 replaced the data.
findings.root_cause: Render metadata is not mechanically bound field-by-field to the attested scientific configuration.
reproduction_steps: Read T001 computed_scope in render_contract.json.
Compare it with parameters.goe and actual_parameters.goe in the v2 config and attestation.
